questions.question: What coat color is this?
questions.explanation: A buckskin can be distinguished from similar colors by its yellow coat and the light hairs in its black mane and tail. Its head may be slightly lighter than its body, whereas a bay’s head is usually the same shade as the body or slightly darker. There is no true black dorsal stripe; if a dark stripe is present, it is broad and diffuse, with no clear edges, and is caused by sooty countershading.

questions.question: What coat color is this?
questions.explanation: Liver chestnut is a dark shade of chestnut. It differs from other chestnut shades only in its darker coat and, occasionally, darker skin.

questions.question: What coat color is this?

questions.explanation: Dappled silver black is easy to identify by the characteristic mottling on the legs and dapples on the body. questions.question: What coat color is this?
questions.explanation: Red roan is easy to identify by the even mixture of white hairs throughout the body coat, while the head, mane, tail, and lower legs remain darker. Unlike light chestnut, the pale appearance comes from a mixture of chestnut and white hairs rather than dilution of the chestnut pigment. It differs from bay roan by the absence of a black mane, tail, and lower legs, and from red dun by the absence of primitive markings: a dark dorsal stripe, leg barring, and a lighter muzzle.

questions.question: What coat color is this?
questions.explanation: Dark gray occurs in young horses and is the first stage of progressive graying. The base coat remains clearly visible and can be any color—black, bay, chestnut, and so on. Graying always begins around the face.

questions.question: What coat color is this?
questions.explanation: Dark bay can sometimes be confused with black or seal brown. When in doubt, check the ears: bays always have black ear rims. Dark bays also have lighter tan areas around the nostrils, which black horses lack. Seal browns have vivid reddish tan points and no tan areas behind the ears or on the belly, whereas dark bays may have these areas and their tan shading may be duller.

questions.question: What coat color is this?
questions.explanation: Grullo is easy to identify by its cool gray or ash-gray body coat combined with primitive markings: a dark dorsal stripe, leg barring, and dark ear rims. Unlike blue roan, the pale appearance comes from the color of each hair rather than a mixture of white hairs, so the body looks uniform. Grullo differs from smoky black by its primitive markings and from dark buckskin by its dorsal stripe and lack of a yellow or sandy cast.

questions.explanation: Rabicano is a pattern in which lighter hairs appear at the tailhead, over the croup, in the groin, and on the belly. The light hairs may extend upward along the sides, forming characteristic white striping over the ribs. Rabicano is often confused with roan, but it is not a form of classic roan.
